Stop treating your payment gateway like a static utility feature. It’s pertinent to ensure you get all your payments on time and that they settle without interruptions. So when thinking about migrating to another payment gateway, don’t treat it like a plumbing issue; you are executing a major financial restructuring.


Right now, your business is likely bleeding margin on hidden FX spreads. Your finance team is suffocating under manual[e-FIRA](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/firc/) reconciliation. Your current provider might be routing export payments without a formal RBI PA-CB license, putting your entire remittance flow at immediate risk of regulatory blockage.


An international payment gateway migration is akin to an infrastructural organ transplant. Get it right, and you instantly improve your unit economics and checkout conversions. Get the routing logic or the recurring data transfer wrong, and your authorisation rates will tank overnight. Delay the project, and you forfeit compounding revenue to operational inefficiencies.


You need to rip out the legacy system and switch to an enterprise-grade stack. This requires aligning your entire C-suite, managing the transition flawlessly, and treating the cutover as a strategic business initiative rather than a simple IT ticket.


##


**What Happens If You Don’t Migrate to a Better International Payment Gateway?**


Executive teams hate migrating payment gateways. Why so?


Well, product managers are terrified of the risks involved, and the engineering team is scared of the integration workload. Consequently, mid-market and enterprise businesses tolerate sub-par payment providers for years.


This complacency carries massive, often unmeasured financial costs. Consider the three silent leaks choking your balance sheet today:


- **The FX Margin Bleed:** Your CFO negotiated a 2.5% processing fee. They completely missed the backend currency conversion spread. Legacy processors force[Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC)](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/apple-pay-with-dynamic-currency-conversion-a-better-checkout-for-global-customers/) , punishing international buyers at checkout. Then they take another margin on the USD to INR settlement. You lose money on both sides.


- **The Compliance Timebomb:** The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) does not deal in grey areas. If your gateway lacks explicit Payment Aggregator – Cross Border (PA-CB) licensing, the authorities will take action. When the regulator cracks down, your remittance channels freeze instantly.


- **The Reconciliation Chokehold:** Processing fifty international orders a month allows for manual Foreign Inward Remittance Advice (FIRA) matching. Scaling to five thousand orders breaks the finance team. They spend weeks chasing AD Category-I banks to prove all inbound capital is legitimate and backed by proper orders.


Switching international payment gateways is the only way to stop these leaks permanently.


##


**The Vendor Evaluation Matrix: Choosing Your Next Payment Gateway Partner**


Audit your target provider ruthlessly before signing a contract. When you decide to change international payment providers, you fundamentally alter the financial ceiling of your business.


Before you select a provider, compare the vendors against the following criteria;


- Do they hold an active, undeniable PA-CB license?
- Ask for the documentation
- Audit their GST compliance


Global gateways operating from outside India often fail to issue proper GST-compliant invoices for their processing fees. If your business cannot claim the 18% GST on processing fees as an Input Tax Credit (ITC), your gateway is artificially inflating your operational costs by at least 20%.


Moreover, you need to ensure the payment gateway you now want to integrate supports Multi-Currency Pricing (MCP).


MCP locks in the FX rate for the merchants. The buyer sees exactly what they will pay in their local currency, and you see exactly what will settle in INR. Zero surprises. This allows direct, predictable settlement without bleeding margin on undisclosed backend currency spreads.


If not for MCP, there is a heightened risk of fraud. High false-positive fraud declines happen when a US transaction hits an Indian acquiring bank. The vendor must intelligently route transactions through local acquiring banks in the buyer’s region (US, EU, MENA) to bypass rigid cross-border risk filters.


Use this exact evaluation matrix when interviewing sales engineers from competing providers:


**Capability Matrix** **Legacy Global Processors** **Enterprise Stack (e.g., Cashfree)** **Business Impact**


**Regulatory Standing** Grey-area cross-border routing. Explicit RBI PA-CB License. Prevents sudden remittance blockages and FEMA audits.


**GST Input Tax Credit** Issues non-compliant international invoices. Issues 18% GST-compliant B2B invoices. Recovers 18% of total processing costs directly to your bottom line.


**Margin Protection** Forces DCC, extracting hidden backend spreads. Natively supports Multi-Currency Pricing (MCP). Locks in merchant FX rates; protects buyer checkout conversion.


**Routing Architecture** Routes all global traffic through Indian acquiring banks. Routes via localised acquiring banks (US, EU, MENA). Bypasses local risk filters, driving double-digit authorisation lifts.


**FIRA Generation** Manual reconciliation via third-party banking portals. Automated e-FIRA generation mapped to RBI Purpose Codes. Eliminates manual accounting hours and ensures export compliance.


Cashfree is an international payment gateway, and we have engineered our cross-border payment stack catering to these local and global realities. This eliminates the gap between Indian compliance and international conversion.


##


**Migration Readiness | Are You Prepared for the Shift?**


A payment migration touches every department. Before you build the payment gateway migration checklist, you must align the internal factions. To ensure every leader is on board, set exact success metrics for each executive leader.


**Leader Position** **Core KPI** **How to Convince Them?**


**Chief Financial Officer (CFO)** Working Capital Velocity
Audit Readiness Show them the math and improvements with a modern and more aligned payment gateway.
Moving away from T+2 or T+3 settlements to Instant or T+1 settlements unlocks trapped working capital.
Prove how automated e-FIRA generation will save the accounting team hundreds of manual hours every quarter and eliminate FEMA violation risks.


**Chief Technology Officer (CTO)** System Uptime
API Latency
PCI Scope Reduction Engineering wants clean documentation and high-fidelity sandbox environments.
Assure the CTO that the new gateway supports secure Vault-to-Vault token transfers. The team will never touch raw PCI data. Establish strict Service Level Agreements (SLAs) for API uptime and webhook delivery.


**VP of Product and CX** Checkout Conversion Rate
APM Coverage Product teams fear conversion drops;
Show them how the new risk engine utilises frictionless 3DS2 to reduce OTP fatigue for low-risk buyers. Map out how the new checkout dynamically displays localised alternative payment methods based on the buyer’s IP address.


##


**Five-Phase International Payment Gateway Migration Process**


###


**Phase 1 – Pre-Migration Compliance and Financial Audit**


Phase one focuses entirely on preparing the financial infrastructure for inbound foreign capital. Manual reconciliation kills scale. You must automate the e-FIRA pipeline immediately.


Execute these specific compliance routing steps before writing your first API call:


- **Map RBI Purpose Codes** : Inside the new merchant dashboard, map your exact product lines to[RBI codes](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/purpose-code-for-international-payments/) . Software and SaaS businesses map payloads directly to P0802 (Software consultancy/implementation). Misclassifying these codes triggers brutal FEMA audits later.


- **Establish the AD Bank Pipe** : Ensure the new gateway routes your settlements through an Authorised Dealer (AD) Category-I bank that supports automated e-FIRA generation via their API.


- **Renegotiate Settlement SLAs** : Stop accepting delayed international settlements as a cost of doing business. Demand faster liquidity. A modern enterprise gateway offers T+0 or T+1 for cross-border flows.


- **Configure Multi-Currency Ledgers** : Refactor your internal database schema to support MCP. Shift from single-currency columns to multi-currency systems.


###


**Phase 2 – Preparing for the Recurring Revenue Model**


Subscriptions and recurring revenue models break during migrations, and they are the hardest ones to maintain after the migration is complete as well. Extracting customer payment data from a legacy vault requires not only operational care, but also complete security, as a single lapse can put the data at risk of unauthorised access.


Since you cannot risk losing Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR), prepare to protect this data at all costs.


- **Card-on-File (CoF) Migration Protocol:** You absolutely cannot export raw credit card data via CSVs Doing so violates PCI-DSS regulations and carries massive fines.


Under the RBI’s Card-on-File Tokenisation (CoFT) rules, you must execute a Vault-to-Vault Token Transfer. The old gateway and the new gateway establish a highly secure, PGP-encrypted communication channel.


They move the network tokens directly between their servers. The merchant will never see or touch the raw PAN (Primary Account Number) data.


Pro tip: ***Ensure your legacy provider contractually agrees to facilitate this transfer without exorbitant hostage fees.***


- **Integrate UPI AutoPay and eNACH Systems**


You cannot always migrate domestic and cross-border recurring mandates silently. The underlying NPCI architecture heavily restricts porting active mandates between aggregators.


To successfully migrate recurring payments, you must engineer a strategic Re-authentication Campaign. Do not wait for the old mandate to fail.


Build an automated flow detecting the legacy mandate, send an in-app push offering a micro-incentive, and route the user through the new gateway’s mandate creation UI.


Here’s an easy map for you to understand exactly what you are migrating based on the payment type:


**Payment Method** **Migration Feasibility** **Technical Execution Path** **Risk Level**


**Credit Cards (International)** High Vault-to-Vault Token Transfer via PGP encryption. Merchant remains out of PCI scope. Low


**Credit Cards (Domestic CoFT)** High Network Tokenization transfer between certified aggregators. Low


**UPI AutoPay** Extremely Low Cannot be ported silently. Requires merchant-led Re-authentication Campaign to capture new mandate. High (Chute drop in active MRR if ignored)


**eNACH / Physical NACH** Low to Zero Requires fresh e-mandate registration via Netbanking/Debit card on the new gateway. High


Also Read:[How Does Payment Gateway Tokenization Work? 3 Types of Token Vault Integration](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/guides/types-of-tokenization-integration/)


###


**Phase 3 – Building the Tech, Mapping Customer Experience, and Sandbox Testing**


Migrations fail in the trailing edge cases. Your development team must treat payment gateway migration testing with extreme caution. Remember, everything that can fail will fail.


Before you launch, execute these steps within the sandbox environment:


- **API & Webhook Parity Normalisation** : Map payload structures line by line. Legacy gateways often use integer-based order IDs, but modern payment gateways like Cashfree use alphanumeric strings.


Write a middleware translation layer to normalise these ID formats before they hit your core database.


If your backend database expects an integer and the new webhook delivers a string, your automated fulfilment logic crashes silently.


- **Alternative Payment Method (APM) Dynamic Rendering:** Credit cards are not enough for global sales. Your tech team needs to re-map localised APMs dynamically.


The checkout UI must render iDEAL for Dutch IP addresses, Pix for Brazilian buyers, and ACH for US enterprise clients.


- **Risk Engine Tuning & Frictionless 3DS2** : Cart abandonment spikes during transitions if the new risk engine is misconfigured or does not account for localisation requirements.


To ensure that does not happen, you need to configure your new provider’s risk parameters to aggressively utilise the[3DS2 frictionless flow](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/international-payments-3ds-2/) .


Cross-border transactions under $30 with matching billing/shipping logic should bypass the OTP challenge entirely. Force the challenge only on high-value or anomalous IP velocity flags.


- **Webhook Polling Fallbacks:** Do not trust webhooks blindly during the cutover. Implement a secondary polling mechanism.


If your server misses the successful webhook from the gateway, a cron job should query the transaction status API every 5 minutes to reconcile dropped states.


###


**Phase 4 – Go Live and Preparing the Rollback Protocol**


To ensure your new international payment gateway starts operating with zero-downtime work with a phased parallel run.


Never flip the switch on 100% of your international traffic overnight.


**The Phased Traffic Split**


- **Day 1 (10% Traffic):** Route 10% of live international traffic to the new gateway. Monitor the exact authorisation rates, latency, and success metrics against your legacy baseline.


- **Day 15 (50% Traffic):** If the financial and technical metrics remain stable, escalate the routing logic to handle half of your global volume.


- **Day 30 (100% Traffic):** Push to full volume. Deprioritise the legacy gateway in the routing layer entirely.


Most important of all, build a Kill Switch. Moreover, define the exact parameters that trigger an immediate and automated rollback to the legacy gateway.


Configure load balancing logic using the following thresholds;


- **Threshold 1 (Latency):** Set a latency kill-switch at 2.5 seconds. If the new API takes longer than 2.5 seconds to return a token creation response, the load balancer must instantly fall back to the old provider.


- **Threshold 2 (Authorisation Drops):** Monitor rolling authorisation rates. If authorisation rates drop by more than 4% against the rolling 7-day average, trigger the rollback.


- **Threshold 3 (Double-Charge Prevention):** Your developers must ensure this failover happens upstream of the final charge execution. If a transaction times out at the acquiring level, failing over blindly will double-charge the end user.


###


**Phase 5 – Reconciliation and 60-Day Sunset Sequence**


Once 100% traffic is routed to the new stack, don’t think the migration process is complete.


Once done, you need to implement the 60-Day Sunset Rule. Keep your legacy gateway active, fully funded, and integrated into your customer support dashboard for exactly 60 days post-cutover.


In our experience with cross-border D2C cutovers, trailing refunds and delayed chargebacks will continue hitting the old Merchant ID (MID) for weeks.


Close the old AD bank routing accounts too early, and those refunds bounce. This triggers manual wire transfers and furious customer support tickets.


Use this window to execute final financial and technical decommissioning:


- Process final trailing refunds originating from the legacy gateway.
- Complete final FIRA matching for past transactions with your old AD bank.
- Scrub your servers of any leftover PCI data tied to the old vault.
- Revoke all legacy API keys from your production and staging environments.
- Officially close the old nodal accounts and sever the routing logic.


##


**Conclusion**


Your payment gateway migration checklist is only complete when the old provider is completely erased from your system architecture. Switching international payment gateways requires total legacy destruction.


Owning your payment stack means controlling your unit economics. Treat compliance routing, APM availability, and FX spreads with identical engineering rigour.


Failing to map an e-FIRA or misconfiguring a recurring token transfer burns capital just as fast as a downed server. Do the math, enforce the fallback protocols, train your stakeholders, and execute the cutover. The cost of standing still is too high.
